Issued at 335 AM EDT Tue Sep 1 2026

Showers have largely diminished across the area early this morning. 
Regional radar mosaic does depict some low coverage showers across 
portions of north central Illinois in what has been a persistent 
zone of westerly flow isentropic upglide from north central Illinois 
into northwest Ohio. One characteristic that has changed over past 6 
to 12 hours is the northeast advection of warmer mid level profiles 
as evident with substantial low level CIN noted per KDVN and KILX 
00Z RAOB from last evening. This west-east oriented zone of 
isentropic forcing will persist through daybreak although in 
terms of mid/upper level forcing, this does appear to coincide 
with a lull. Did maintain some 15-20 PoPs across the northern 
third into mid morning, but weak mid/upper level forcing and 
somewhat more unfavorable mid level thermal profiles should keep
coverage very low if any showers are able to develop.

For this afternoon, some sheared vorticity associated with stronger 
northern latitude westerlies will top the upper ridge and begin to 
shift east across the western/southern Great Lakes late this 
afternoon into early this evening.  Primary surface boundary will be 
displaced well to the northwest but strong buoyancy is expected to 
develop in pre-frontal environment from northeast IL eastward 
into southern Lower MI/far northern IN (MLCAPEs around 3000 J/kg 
possible). The more robust shear profiles should be displaced 
closer to main sfc boundary across, but deep layer shear 
magnitudes on the order of 25 to 35 knots will likely have a 
narrow spatial overlay with this stronger buoyancy north of the 
US Route 30 corridor. The very warm mid level profiles in place 
raise some question as to the potential of surface based CIN 
lingering in the afternoon, although with the very warm/moist 
near sfc airmass in place, would suspect this CIN will be 
minimal during peak hating. What appears to be a large component
missing today from an appreciable severe threat is any 
pronounced stronger pre-frontal convergence or trigger 
mechanism. Aforementioned shear vorticity max will likely be 
migrating northward across east central WI/central Lower MI 
later this afternoon/evening, with not a great juxtaposition of
forcing and better shear/instability. A Marginal Risk of severe
weather has been maintained today for areas roughly north of US
Route 30 corridor which seems reasonable given 
shear/instability combination. Some persistent isentropic 
upglide in 310-315k layer persists today which could aid in 
initiation, but overall weak nature to mid/upper level forcing 
continues to suggest very low confidence in severe weather 
occurrence today.

For most, the main weather concern today will be high heat and 
humidity, with warm/moist airmass now firmly in place across the 
region. Given aforementioned warmer mid level profiles and lack of 
clear upstream wave early in the day, better insolation should be 
realized today in comparison to past few days with most areas 
reaching around 90 or lower 90s for highs. Dew points should be 
fairly uniform in low to possibly mid 70s across the area which 
will produce heat indices in the upper 90s to around 105. Given 
continued low confidence in coverage of showers/storms even across 
the north today, derived heat indices from this morning's forecast 
grids show rather minimal differences across the area with peak 
afternoon heat indices. Given Wednesday should feature even greater 
confidence in reaching advisory criteria area-wide, did go ahead and 
extend the pre-existing Heat Advisory across the remainder of 
southern Lower Michigan in effect from 18Z today to 00Z Wednesday 
evening for all areas. Have not expanded this advisory into 
Thursday yet, but the possibility exists that areas roughly 
along and south of US 30 may need the Heat Advisory extended 
into early Thursday evening.

In addition to the ongoing heat concerns for Wednesday, 
convective potential will once again need to be watched for 
afternoon/evening. The larger scale primary upper trough will be
tracking across western Quebec Wed afternoon but another short 
wave will be exiting out of the Dakotas with a secondary 
northward surge of a low level theta-e ridge across Upper 
Midwest/Corn Belt. Synoptic pattern would tend to favor frontal 
boundary position north of the local area into early Wednesday 
evening, but if a more organized area of storms can form across 
Upper Midwest/Corn Belt Wednesday at nose of this secondary
theta-e max, it is possible associated outflow could modulate 
position of this boundary to the southern Lower Michigan by 
evening. In any event, stronger mid/upper level forcing still 
looks to bypass the area to the north, and isolated severe 
threat may require this southward modulation of effective 
frontal boundary by upstream outflow which is of course of low
